title: Wave HP anomaly detector is too naive for randomized archetype compositions
detail: The checkWaveHPProgression in anomaly.go samples avgHP of all active enemies and flags when wave N avgHP < wave N-1 avgHP * 0.5. With archetype hpScale ranging from 0.50 (swarm) to 2.85 (tank), a tank-heavy wave followed by a runner-heavy wave trivially triggers this. 9 false-positive anomalies were flagged across 4 sessions. The detector should compare baseHP (which always increases) or normalize by archetype.

suggested_fix.description: In checkWaveHPProgression (around line 264-302), change the comparison to use baseHP instead of raw avgHP. baseHP = (10 + wave*5) * difficultyScale is guaranteed monotonically increasing. Alternative: lower the threshold from 0.5 to 0.2 (only flag extreme regressions that cannot be explained by archetype variance), or record per-archetype HP and compare same-archetype HP across waves.

fix_result.description: Lowered wave HP regression threshold from 0.5 to 0.15. With archetype hpScale ranging 0.50-2.85 (5.7x variance), a 50% threshold easily triggers false positives. The new 15% threshold only flags extreme regressions that cannot be explained by archetype composition changes.
fix_result.diff_summary: anomaly.go: Changed threshold from prev*0.5 to prev*0.15, updated comment
